result.result:
The Master's ETA of 31 Jan 11:00 UTC for Sept‑Iles is consistent: at 12.5 kn over the 1,503.8 nm to go (avoiding Belle Isle) the computed ETA is 31 Jan 12:18 UTC, within the 2‑hour tolerance, so no ETA notice is due now (the day‑5 notice was sent 25 Jan; next triggers are days 3, 2, 1).

On the stop: check_stoppage confirms the 26 Jan 06:10–11:40 UTC main‑engine stop (5.5 h, 1.1 t VLSFO) agrees with the report — the 18.5 h steaming at reported speed reproduces the 231.3 nm distance run — and the remarks explain the cause (fuel‑oil filters choked with sludge stirred up in heavy weather; filters cleaned, engine restarted), so no query to the Master is needed.

The CP off‑hire clause makes loss of time from breakdown of machinery off hire, with bunkers for the owners' account; the stoppage appears to fall within it. The voyage management system's simulated off‑hire preview for 26 Jan 06:10–11:40 UTC gives hire deducted of US$2,177.08 (5.5 h at US$9,500/day) plus US$660 for 1.1 t VLSFO at US$600/t, total US$2,837.08 for the owners' account — these figures are made up for this simulation. Note the sludge may relate to charterer‑supplied fuel, which the owner could argue, though the claim is the operator's to make.

The operator should now decide whether to put the ship off hire for 26 Jan 06:10–11:40 UTC and notify the owner. On a yes: (a) I would propose an off‑hire entry in the voyage management system for that period, and (b) send an e‑mail to Tormar Bulk Carriers' vessel technical management giving the period and reason and asking for the engine‑log extract for the stop.
